description: Designing digital integrated circuits from the MOS transistor up: CMOS logic, fabrication and layout rules, delay, power and timing, combinational and sequential subsystems, hardware description languages, the FPGA design flow and design for testability. Circuits are described in Verilog, simulated and synthesised in the browser, and laid out and timed until a small design passes its rule checks and tests.
modelledOn: Weste and Harris, CMOS VLSI Design: A Circuits and Systems Perspective
Rabaey, Chandrakasan and Nikolic, Digital Integrated Circuits: A Design Perspective
IEEE 1364 Verilog and IEEE 1800 SystemVerilog hardware description language standards
IEEE 1149.1 Standard Test Access Port and Boundary-Scan Architecture
outcomes: Explain MOS transistor operation and analyse the static and dynamic behaviour of the CMOS inverter.
Design static and dynamic CMOS gates and draw their stick diagrams and layouts within design rules.
Estimate delay with RC and logical-effort models, analyse power dissipation and apply low-power techniques.
Describe, simulate and synthesise combinational and sequential designs in Verilog and take them through an FPGA flow to timing closure.
Apply fault models, scan design and built-in self-test to make a design testable.

units.title: MOS transistors and the CMOS inverter
topics: Integrated circuit history, scaling and Moore's law; design hierarchy and abstraction levels
MOS structure, threshold voltage and the long-channel I-V model
Non-ideal effects: velocity saturation, channel-length modulation, body effect, subthreshold and gate leakage
The CMOS inverter: voltage transfer characteristic, noise margins and beta ratio
Switching behaviour of the inverter; load capacitance

units.title: CMOS logic
topics: Static CMOS: complementary pull-up and pull-down networks; NAND, NOR and compound AOI and OAI gates
Transmission gates and pass-transistor logic; multiplexers
Ratioed logic and pseudo-NMOS
Dynamic and domino logic; charge sharing and keepers
Stick diagrams and Euler paths for gate layout

units.title: Fabrication and layout rules
topics: Wafer preparation, oxidation, photolithography, doping, etching and metallisation
The CMOS process flow: n-well and twin-well processes; interconnect layers and vias
Lambda-based and micron design rules; latch-up and guard rings
Layout of an inverter and a NAND gate; standard-cell layout conventions
Design rule checking, layout-versus-schematic and parasitic extraction
Process variation, corners and yield

units.title: Timing and delay
topics: RC delay models and the Elmore delay
Logical effort: gate sizing and choosing the best number of stages
Interconnect: wire resistance and capacitance, crosstalk and repeater insertion
Static timing analysis: setup and hold constraints, critical paths, clock skew and jitter

units.title: Power
topics: Dynamic switching power, short-circuit power and static leakage
Activity factors and power estimation
Low-power techniques: clock gating, power gating, multiple threshold voltages, dynamic voltage and frequency scaling
Energy-delay trade-offs; designing chips for battery-powered and off-grid devices

units.title: Combinational and sequential subsystems
topics: Static and dynamic latches and flip-flops in CMOS; sequencing overhead
Clock generation and distribution: H-trees, clock skew management, PLLs in brief
Datapath subsystems: ripple, carry-lookahead and prefix adders; array and Booth multipliers; shifters
Memory arrays: the 6T SRAM cell, DRAM, sense amplifiers and decoders
Pipelining a datapath to meet a clock target

units.title: Hardware description languages
topics: Verilog modules, ports, data types and continuous assignment
Procedural blocks: combinational and clocked always blocks; blocking versus non-blocking assignment
Finite state machines in Verilog; parameterised and hierarchical designs
Testbenches, stimulus generation, self-checking tests and waveform debugging
Writing synthesisable code: inferred latches, resets and coding pitfalls
VHDL and SystemVerilog compared in brief

units.title: FPGA design flow
topics: FPGA architecture: look-up tables, configurable logic blocks, routing, block RAM and DSP slices
The flow: synthesis, technology mapping, placement, routing and bitstream generation
Timing constraints, timing reports and achieving timing closure
ASIC and FPGA flows compared: cost, volume, performance and time to market
Project: a UART and a prepaid electricity meter controller implemented on a simulated FPGA

units.title: Testing and design for testability
topics: Manufacturing test versus functional verification; defects and yield
Fault models: stuck-at, transition and bridging faults; fault coverage
Automatic test pattern generation and the D-algorithm
Controllability and observability; scan chains and scan design
Built-in self-test with LFSRs and MISRs
Boundary scan and the JTAG test access port

schedule.title: Scaling and the MOS transistor
schedule.exercise: Plot transistor counts against years from five chips on a log scale, fit a doubling time, and write what limits further scaling.

tasks.title: Sweep gate voltage on an NMOS transistor, plot drain current, and read off the threshold voltage from the curve
Plot the output characteristics of an NMOS at four gate voltages and mark the linear and saturation regions with the long-channel model
Compare long-channel and velocity-saturated current for a short device, and estimate the subthreshold leakage at three threshold voltages

schedule.title: The CMOS inverter
schedule.exercise: Derive the switching threshold of an inverter from equal currents in both transistors, and show how the beta ratio moves it.

tasks.title: Plot the voltage transfer characteristic of a CMOS inverter and read off the switching threshold
Find noise margins from the transfer curve for beta ratios 1, 2 and 3 and choose the ratio that balances them
Measure propagation delay of an inverter driving loads of 10, 50 and 100 fF and relate the delay to the load capacitance

schedule.title: Logic styles and layout planning
schedule.exercise: Design the pull-up and pull-down networks for a given function by hand and check that the networks are exact complements.

tasks.title: Build a static CMOS NAND and a NOR gate from transistors and verify every row of their truth tables
Build the compound gate for an AOI22 function as one static CMOS stage and verify all 16 input combinations
Build a domino AND gate, show charge sharing corrupting its output, and fix it with a keeper transistor

schedule.title: Fabrication and design rules
schedule.exercise: Explain in order the steps from bare wafer to a working transistor, and say which step defines the gate length.

tasks.title: Step through the CMOS fabrication sequence and record which layers each step adds or removes
Step through an n-well process cross-section and label substrate, well, gate, source, drain and contact at each stage
Check a hand layout against lambda-based design rules, find the violations, and explain the latch-up risk and where guard rings go

schedule.title: Layout and variation
schedule.exercise: Sketch the layout of a NAND gate on a standard cell grid, stating its height, power rails and pin positions.

tasks.title: Draw the stick diagram of an inverter and a NAND gate and check that the layout matches the schematic
Run a layout-versus-schematic comparison on a cell with a planted missing contact and fix the error
Simulate a gate at slow, typical and fast corners with temperature and voltage variation and report the spread of delay

schedule.title: Delay, logical effort and timing
schedule.exercise: Use logical effort to size a chain of gates driving a large load and compare the delay with equal sizing.

tasks.title: Compute the Elmore delay of a four-stage RC ladder by hand and compare it with the simulated 50 percent delay
Size a chain of inverters to drive a 100 times larger load with logical effort and verify the minimum delay by simulation
Find the critical path of a small pipelined datapath, compute setup and hold slack with clock skew, and fix a hold violation

schedule.title: Power and low-power design
schedule.exercise: Calculate the dynamic and leakage power of a chip block from given activity, frequency, capacitance and voltage, and show where the budget is spent.

tasks.title: Measure the switching power of an inverter at three clock rates and check it against C times V squared times f
Add clock gating to a register bank, measure the power with and without it for low activity, and report the saving
Choose the supply voltage and frequency of a battery-powered sensor chip to minimise energy per operation under a deadline

schedule.title: Sequential and datapath circuits
schedule.exercise: Compare ripple-carry and carry-lookahead adders for 16 bits in terms of delay and gate count with a short table.

tasks.title: Build a master-slave flip-flop from latches and verify the clocked behaviour on a test pattern
Build a 4-bit carry-lookahead adder and compare its worst-case delay with a ripple-carry adder on the same inputs
Pipeline a 32-bit multiplier datapath to meet a clock target and report the added latency, registers and throughput gain

schedule.title: Verilog fundamentals
schedule.exercise: Predict by hand the output of three small Verilog blocks that mix blocking and non-blocking assignments, then check by simulation.

tasks.title: Write a Verilog module for a 4-bit adder with continuous assignment and test it against five input pairs
Write combinational and clocked always blocks for a multiplexer and a counter, using the right assignment style, and test both
Design a parameterised finite state machine for a prepaid meter token check in Verilog and verify it on its timing diagram

schedule.title: Testbenches and synthesis
schedule.exercise: Review a given Verilog file and mark every coding pitfall that would make synthesis produce a latch or a wrong reset.

tasks.title: Write a testbench for a counter that applies clock and reset, and read the waveform to find the count at 10 cycles
Write a self-checking testbench for a 4-bit adder that compares every sum with a reference and prints the number of failures
Find and fix an inferred latch and a missing-reset bug in a faulty Verilog design, and show the corrected waveform

schedule.title: FPGA architecture and timing
schedule.exercise: Draw how a 4-input look-up table implements any function of four variables and give the truth table content for a parity function.

tasks.title: Program a look-up table to implement a 3-input majority function and check all eight inputs
Step through synthesis, mapping, placement and routing for a small design and record the resources used at each stage
Read a timing report for a design that misses its clock, find the critical path, and change the design to reach timing closure

schedule.title: ASIC versus FPGA and the project
schedule.exercise: Project report: explain the UART and meter controller design, show the simulation results, and compare cost and speed with an ASIC route.

tasks.title: Compare ASIC and FPGA routes for a product at 1000 and 1 million units using a cost model, and choose one with reasons
Build a UART transmitter as a state machine, send one byte, and check the start bit, data bits and stop bit on the waveform
Implement a prepaid electricity meter controller with a UART interface on a simulated FPGA and test top-up, consumption and low-credit cases

schedule.title: Testing and design for test
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page note on why a chip that passes functional verification can still fail manufacturing test.

tasks.title: Apply stuck-at faults to a small circuit and list which input vectors detect each fault
Insert a scan chain in a small sequential circuit and show how shifting in a pattern gives control of internal state
Build a 4-bit LFSR pattern generator and a signature register, inject a fault, and show that the signature differs from the good one
